findings.title: Answer positions allow content-free readiness
All multi-response items have too few options
Topic membership is mistaken for objective-level evidence
CLF full mocks cannot meet the security weight
Linear scaled-score conversion produces an unjustified pass line
The timed mode prevents real exam navigation and reallocating time
Covered flags exceed the demonstrated teaching and testing
RDS Multi-AZ comparisons need deployment-type scope
Permissions boundaries are not an unconditional ceiling on every grant
Public internet NAT is not the behavior of every NAT gateway
Snow recommendations omit restrictions already in effect
ALB only healthy targets ignores fail-open behavior
Lifecycle requirements should not imply a last-access trigger
The replication lab omits mandatory prerequisites and retention controls
Route 53 policies select DNS responses, not exact user request percentages
Kinesis ordering is not a single total order across a stream
DAX microsecond responses need a cache/consistency qualification
DynamoDB on-demand is automatic but not unbounded
A presigned URL is transferable bearer access
VPC survival and no-inbound assertions are not proven by the checklist
The SQS lab omits acknowledgement and retention limits
Budget alerts and tags need implementation qualifications
Visual fact manifests cite internal notes rather than independent authority
A data-sovereignty requirement does not necessarily require multiple Regions
Exposure is not unseen performance or recency
The existing exam/readiness suite currently fails
Spot is not an unconditional lowest-compute-cost guarantee
Only 96 of the 120 SAA-eligible questions can enter full mocks
